analysis.title: GS US TMT .. Apple (AAPL) - does it get defended or not?
key_insights: Apple is down about 4% pre-market after its results. The desk calls 'does the dip get bought or not' the number one debate of the day.

NDX futures are up 65 bps to start as the NDX tries to bounce off its 200-day moving average after a roughly 275 bps intraday drop yesterday. Crude is moving toward about $100, and yesterday's oil drop only helped the consumer discretionary parts of tech.

The desk treats Apple as a tell on risk appetite. Apple has seemingly become a proxy for anti-AI / NDX trading, so a bought dip could indicate still-muted risk appetite for AI infrastructure and semis.

Bull case: iPhone revenue was up 17% y/y in September and December-quarter total revenue is guided up 7-10% y/y. The desk also cites the early stage of a big product cycle (Duo / foldable, touchable MacBook), strong capital returns and FCF yield, and Apple's privacy, distribution and scale advantages for delivering AI to consumers.

Bear case: Services is guided up 8-9% y/y for the December quarter on mobile gaming softness, third-party licensing (TAC) headwinds and App Store changes such as US link-out transactions. That points to a mix-shift headwind as high-margin Services decelerates.

Gross margin headwinds are emerging as the benefit from lower-cost carry-in memory inventory and tariff refunds fades. Server-side inference costs for Siri AI could also be recognized in Services COGS, and Apple's ability to compete in consumer AI tooling is still to be determined.

GIR (Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research) keeps its Buy rating on Apple. Estimates fall about 2% overnight to about $9 EPS in FY27 and about $10 in FY28 on margin compression from supply constraints, while GIR has more confidence in the iPhone refresh cycle.
Apple's forward P/E is about 35x versus about 19x for the NDX, a historically wide gap. Apple's FCF yield is on trend with the NDX and slightly better.

The desk says it is a healthy debate whether FY26 will be remembered as peak gross margins for Apple, given some one-time tariff refund benefit. The alternative is that a Services re-acceleration keeps pushing corporate gross margins higher.
GIR mutual fund positioning data shows Apple as a consistent underweight. Hedge fund conversations suggest lukewarm sentiment, and Apple short interest is elevated but off the highs.
The dialogue resembles the one about 90 days ago after fiscal Q3 results. That dip was short-lived as Apple became negatively correlated to the NDX and traded as a low-vol, safe-haven proxy.

Other overnight pre-market moves: SHOP -16%, DT -15%, ZBRA -14%, IT -7%, PLTR -6%. Top client inbounds cover whether PLTR gets defended, the ON rally of about 8% from post-print lows, software weakness (DT, NOW, ZS, TWLO), and earnings set-ups led by AMD.
Events today: US midterm elections, JOLTS data, and the SNOW CEO keynote at 1pm ET. After-close earnings include ALAB, AMD, ANET, BKNG, CPNG, DUOL, TOST and XYZ.

AAPL guided December-quarter total revenue up 7-10% y/y and Services revenue up 8-9% y/y. The guide cites mobile gaming softness, third-party licensing (TAC) headwinds and App Store structural shifts.
GIR cut its AAPL EPS estimates about 2% after the print, to about $9 for FY27 and about $10 for FY28, on margin compression from supply constraints.

risk_factors: Services mix-shift: Services growth guided to 8-9% y/y for the December quarter on mobile gaming softness, TAC headwinds and US App Store link-out transactions.
Gross margin pressure as lower-cost memory inventory and tariff refund benefits wane, and supply constraints compress margins.
Server-side inference costs from the Siri AI rollout could be recognized in Services COGS.
Apple's ability to compete and serve AI tooling to consumers is still undetermined.
The dip may fail to be bought, which would signal weak risk appetite, and Apple's trading as an anti-AI proxy complicates the read.

Hedge fund conversations suggest Apple sentiment has been more lukewarm.
Apple has become negatively correlated to the NDX and trades as a low-vol, safe-haven proxy, per the desk's description of the post-F3Q dip.

tension_points.bull_case: iPhone revenue was up 17% y/y in September and December total revenue is guided up 7-10% y/y. The early product cycle (Duo / foldable, touchable MacBook), strong capital returns and FCF yield, and a privacy, distribution and scale edge for consumer AI back the stock. The Services and gross margin concerns are described as 'bad news' already in the stock.
tension_points.bear_case: Services is guided up only 8-9% y/y, so high-margin mix shifts against Apple. Gross margins face pressure as cheap memory inventory and tariff refunds fade, Siri AI inference costs may land in Services COGS, and Apple's ability to compete in consumer AI is unresolved.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The desk's marker is whether the dip gets bought today. A repeat of the short-lived dip after F3Q results, rather than a durable bounce, would favor the bear case.
